note: The 90 exam-English words and phrases of LEARNING.md section 4.6. 'signals' is an exam heuristic, not an AWS fact: keywords are also used as bait, so read every constraint. Stem fragments are original.

items.meaning: the cheapest option that still meets every requirement
items.signals: first reject every option that fails a requirement, then pick the cheapest of the rest
items.stem: Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

items.meaning: the team does the least work to run it
items.signals: a managed or serverless feature, not scripts or software on instances
items.stem: Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

items.meaning: the strongest protection among options that work
items.signals: least privilege, temporary credentials and private access, even when another option is cheaper
items.stem: Which solution will provide access in the MOST secure way?

items.meaning: it keeps working when one part fails; this book: a short interruption is acceptable
items.signals: more than one Availability Zone, a load balancer or automatic failover
items.stem: The company needs a highly available architecture for the web tier.

items.meaning: it keeps working when one part fails; this book: with no interruption
items.signals: stronger than highly available in this book: spare capacity is already running
items.stem: The application must be fault tolerant if one Availability Zone becomes unavailable.

items.meaning: it recovers from failure best
items.signals: remove single points of failure and automate recovery
items.stem: Which design is the MOST resilient to the failure of an Availability Zone?

items.meaning: the shortest wait for a response
items.signals: move data or compute closer to the user: caching, edge services, the nearest Region
items.stem: Users around the world need the LOWEST latency when they load the images.

items.meaning: it meets the need with the least ongoing work and fewest moving parts
items.signals: a built-in feature of the service, not a custom solution
items.stem: What is the MOST operationally efficient way to collect the logs?

items.meaning: the developers write or change the least code
items.signals: a configuration change or a compatible managed service, not a redesign
items.stem: Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

items.meaning: it can handle more load when the load grows
items.signals: automatic scaling or a service that scales without capacity planning
items.stem: The company needs a scalable solution that handles the growth in traffic.

items.meaning: sometimes, not regularly
items.signals: pay per use; not instances that run all the time
items.stem: The application receives sporadic requests during the day.

items.meaning: it starts and stops, with pauses between
items.signals: capacity that can pause or scale to zero; pay per use
items.stem: The reporting database has intermittent usage and is idle most of the night.

items.meaning: you cannot plan the load
items.signals: automatic scaling, on-demand capacity, or a queue as a buffer
items.stem: Traffic to the new application is unpredictable.

items.meaning: the load jumps up quickly for a short time
items.signals: a buffer in front of slow parts, and scaling that reacts fast
items.stem: The order service has sudden spikes in traffic during sales events.

items.meaning: the same load all the time
items.signals: a commitment discount or provisioned capacity
items.stem: The production instances have steady-state usage all year.

items.meaning: you know the load in advance
items.signals: scheduled scaling or a commitment; no need for the most flexible option
items.stem: The batch job runs on a predictable schedule every night.

items.meaning: one job runs for a long time
items.signals: check the maximum run time of the compute option; containers or instances fit long jobs
items.stem: Each long-running job processes one large video file.

items.meaning: each job finishes quickly
items.signals: functions that start on an event
items.stem: The short-lived tasks start when a file arrives.

items.meaning: the application keeps no memory between requests
items.signals: any instance can serve any request, so instances can be added, removed or interrupted
items.stem: The stateless web tier runs on instances behind a load balancer.

items.meaning: stopping the work and starting it again is acceptable
items.signals: spare capacity at a discount that AWS can take back
items.stem: The image-processing jobs can tolerate interruption and can be restarted.

items.meaning: it is a hard requirement
items.signals: an option that does not meet it is wrong, even if the option is cheaper or easier
items.stem: All data must be encrypted before the data leaves the application.

items.meaning: very demanding
items.signals: the strongest control, not the cheapest
items.stem: The company has stringent compliance requirements for audit logs.

items.meaning: a rule from outside the team requires it
items.signals: treat it as a hard constraint, and prefer a control that enforces it centrally
items.stem: A security policy mandates that no instance has a public IP address.

items.meaning: make it certain
items.signals: a hard requirement; if an action must not happen, prevent it, not only alert
items.stem: The architect must ensure that objects cannot be deleted for one year.

items.meaning: the business stops if it fails
items.signals: pay for availability and fast recovery; the cheapest design is probably wrong
items.stem: The company runs a mission-critical order database.

items.meaning: the business allows it
items.signals: a relaxed requirement: a cheaper or simpler option is now allowed
items.stem: A delay of several hours to retrieve the files is acceptable.

items.meaning: this much or more
items.signals: a lower limit: check that capacity or retention never falls below it
items.stem: The company must keep the logs for at least 7 years.

items.meaning: the company does not accept this
items.signals: remove every option that includes the unwanted thing
items.stem: The company wants to avoid managing any servers.

items.meaning: enough for the need
items.signals: do not choose more than is needed; the larger option costs more
items.stem: A recovery time of several hours is sufficient for the test environment.

items.meaning: with the shortest delay
items.signals: the fastest option that meets the other constraints; watch the transfer or retrieval time
items.stem: The company must move the data to AWS as soon as possible.

items.meaning: with no noticeable delay
items.signals: the smallest delay; a reading rule of this book, compare with near real-time
items.stem: The dashboard must show the sensor readings in real time.

items.meaning: a short delay is acceptable
items.signals: a short delay is allowed, so a service that buffers data can fit
items.stem: The clickstream data must be available for analysis in near real-time.

items.meaning: people read the data only sometimes
items.signals: a cheaper storage class; check the retrieval charge and how fast a read must be
items.stem: After 30 days, the documents are infrequently accessed.

items.meaning: nobody can change or delete the data
items.signals: a lock that prevents changes, not only versioning
items.stem: Regulations require that the records are immutable for 5 years.

items.meaning: keep the data for a set time
items.signals: lifecycle rules and retention settings; count the required period
items.stem: The company must retain the backups for 90 days.

items.meaning: store data for a long time and read it almost never
items.signals: the coldest storage that still meets the retrieval time in the stem
items.stem: The company wants to archive the audio files for 7 years.

items.meaning: the data is not lost
items.signals: storage that keeps copies in several places; durability is not the same as availability
items.stem: The uploaded files must be stored in a highly durable way.

items.meaning: the state of the data at one exact moment
items.signals: continuous backups or snapshots; check how far back and how exact
items.stem: The team must restore the database to a point in time before the error.

items.meaning: after some time, not maybe
items.signals: a short delay before all readers see a change is acceptable
items.stem: The replicas are eventually consistent with the primary.

items.meaning: several changes succeed together or fail together
items.signals: a database with ACID transactions: a relational engine, or Amazon DynamoDB transactions
items.stem: The application runs transactional queries with joins across many tables.

items.meaning: AWS does the operating work
items.signals: choose the AWS service over the same software installed on instances
items.stem: The company wants a fully managed message broker.

items.meaning: no servers for the team to manage or size
items.signals: functions, managed containers without instances, and on-demand data services
items.stem: The company wants a serverless solution for the new API.

items.meaning: create and size a resource in advance
items.signals: provisioned means capacity you choose and pay for; the opposite is on-demand
items.stem: The team does not want to provision capacity for peak load.

items.meaning: install software fixes
items.signals: work the team wants to give away: a managed service, or an automated patch tool
items.stem: The operations team spends too much time on patching the database servers.

items.meaning: make it happen without a person
items.signals: a built-in schedule, rule or policy, not a manual runbook
items.stem: The company wants to automate the rotation of database credentials.

items.meaning: separate two parts so one keeps working when the other is slow or fails
items.signals: a queue, a topic or an event bus between the parts
items.stem: A solutions architect must decouple the web tier from the processing tier.

items.meaning: run several steps in order, with retries and decisions
items.signals: a workflow service, not code that calls each step by hand
items.stem: The company needs to orchestrate a multi-step order workflow.

items.meaning: control many accounts or resources from one place
items.signals: an organization-wide service or policy, not a setting repeated in each account
items.stem: The security team wants to centrally manage firewall rules across all accounts.

items.meaning: watch and be told when something happens
items.signals: metrics and alarms for performance; an audit trail for who did what
items.stem: The team wants to monitor CPU usage and be notified of high values.

items.meaning: few people run the system
items.signals: the same as least operational overhead: prefer managed services
items.stem: The startup has a small team with no experience in running Kubernetes.

items.meaning: only the permissions that the task needs
items.signals: a narrow policy on a role; never broad permissions or shared credentials
items.stem: The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

items.meaning: while the data is stored
items.signals: storage encryption with a key service; check who must control the key
items.stem: All data must be encrypted at rest.

items.meaning: while the data moves over a network
items.signals: TLS and certificates; check whether requests that are not encrypted must be refused
items.stem: The company must encrypt the data in transit between the application and the database.

items.meaning: replace a key or a password with a new one on a schedule
items.signals: a secrets service with built-in rotation, not a script
items.stem: The database password must be rotated every 30 days.

items.meaning: keep a record of who did what and when
items.signals: the API activity trail and the configuration history, not performance metrics
items.stem: An auditor must see who deleted the security group.

items.meaning: allow only some people or networks
items.signals: a policy condition, a resource-based policy or a network rule that names what is allowed
items.stem: The company must restrict access to the bucket to one VPC.

items.meaning: data that causes harm if other people see it
items.signals: encryption, tight access, and a service that discovers such data
items.stem: The bucket stores sensitive customer documents.

items.meaning: keep apart so that one cannot reach the other
items.signals: separate accounts, VPCs, subnets or security groups, by how strong the isolation must be
items.stem: The company must isolate the production workload from development.

items.meaning: it stops working after a set time
items.signals: roles and temporary credentials, or a time-limited link; never long-term keys
items.stem: External auditors need temporary access to the reports.

items.meaning: the company, not AWS, controls the encryption keys
items.signals: customer managed keys in a key service; check who must control rotation
items.stem: The company must manage its own encryption keys and control their rotation.

items.meaning: in the company's own data center, not in AWS
items.signals: a hybrid question: think about the network link, the transfer tool and where identities live
items.stem: The company runs an application on premises and wants to back up the data to AWS.

also: both on premises and in AWS
items.meaning: AWS and the data center work together
items.signals: private connectivity, and services that extend AWS storage or identity to the data center
items.stem: The company needs a hybrid storage solution for its file servers.

items.meaning: the traffic stays off the public internet
items.signals: VPC endpoints inside AWS; a dedicated or private link from outside
items.stem: The instances must access the service privately, without traversing the internet.

items.meaning: users on the internet reach it directly
items.signals: a public entry point with protection in front; the tiers behind it stay private
items.stem: The company hosts an internet-facing web application.

items.meaning: users are far from one Region
items.signals: edge caching, global routing or more than one Region
items.stem: Users around the world report slow downloads of static content.

items.meaning: copies or capacity in more than one zone of one Region
items.signals: protection against a zone failure; not protection against a Region failure
items.stem: The instances run across multiple Availability Zones.

items.meaning: between two Regions
items.signals: disaster recovery or global users; replication features and their cost
items.stem: The company requires cross-Region disaster recovery for the database.

items.meaning: a private network line that only this company uses
items.signals: a dedicated physical link, compared with a VPN that runs over the internet
items.stem: The company needs a dedicated connection with consistent network performance.

items.meaning: at AWS sites near the users
items.signals: content delivery and protection before traffic reaches the Region
items.stem: The company wants to block malicious requests at the edge.

items.meaning: the law says where the data is stored
items.signals: keep data and backups in the named Region; reject options that copy data elsewhere
items.stem: Because of data residency rules, the data must remain in one Region.

items.meaning: move an application or data to AWS
items.signals: find the size, the time limit and the network link; they decide the tool
items.stem: A company plans to migrate 60 TB of data to Amazon S3.

items.meaning: move the application without changing it
items.signals: instances and a rehosting tool, not a new serverless design
items.stem: The company wants to lift and shift the application to AWS.

items.meaning: keep the code as it is
items.signals: a compatible managed service or a change in configuration, not a redesign
items.stem: The company needs higher availability without changing the application.

items.meaning: small code changes are acceptable
items.signals: a service with a compatible interface; reject a full rewrite
items.stem: The solution must require minimal code changes.

items.meaning: change the design of the application
items.signals: the stem allows new services such as functions, queues or containers
items.stem: The company is willing to refactor the application to reduce cost.

items.meaning: an old system that is hard to change
items.signals: keep its protocols and interfaces; prefer services that support them
items.stem: A legacy application uses a standard messaging protocol.

items.meaning: one large application where all parts depend on each other
items.signals: a question about splitting it or decoupling its parts
items.stem: The company runs a monolithic application on one large instance.

items.meaning: the system stops for a very short time or not at all
items.signals: replication before the switch, not a backup and restore
items.stem: The database migration must have minimal downtime.

items.meaning: changes keep flowing from the source to the target
items.signals: a replication or change-data-capture feature, not a one-time copy
items.stem: The company needs ongoing replication from the source database until the cutover.

items.meaning: it happens once
items.signals: no need for a permanent link or service; compare transfer time with a shipped device
items.stem: The company needs a one-time transfer of archived video files.

items.word: Which solution will meet these requirements?
items.meaning: choose the one option that satisfies every requirement in the stem
items.signals: list the requirements first; an option that misses one requirement is wrong
items.stem: Which solution will meet these requirements?

items.meaning: all the needs stated before the question
items.signals: go back and count them; there are often two or three
items.stem: What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

items.meaning: exactly that number of options are correct
items.signals: judge each option as true or false on its own, then count that you marked the right number
items.stem: Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

items.meaning: the correct options work together as one solution
items.signals: the chosen options must not conflict; often one is the service and one is its configuration
items.stem: Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take?

items.meaning: often more than one option works; rank the options that work
items.signals: the capital word names the ranking rule; find it before reading the options
items.stem: Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?

items.meaning: the option that fits the stated requirements most completely
items.signals: several options are possible; the stem's constraints decide, not your preference
items.stem: Which storage solution BEST meets these requirements?

items.meaning: how the system is now
items.signals: the starting point; the answer changes as little of it as the requirements allow
items.stem: The company currently stores the files on an EC2 instance.

items.meaning: the goal of the company
items.signals: the sentence with this phrase usually holds the requirement
items.stem: The company wants to reduce the load on the primary database.

items.meaning: a requirement, as strong as must
items.signals: treat it as a hard constraint
items.stem: A solutions architect needs to design a solution that scales automatically.

items.meaning: a problem or a change follows
items.signals: the sentence after it describes what is wrong; the answer fixes that one thing
items.stem: However, users report errors during peak hours.
